text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The purchase of Polish Investment Bank (PBI) by Kredyt Bank was taken into consideration when the latter planned its upcoming share issue, so the deal should not affect Kredyt's 1997 financial results, Kredyt president Stanislaw Pacuk said.
The bank expects a net profit of 42 million zlotys in 1997.

- Poland's WSK PZL-Mielec aircraft maker and the U.S.'s Lockheed Martin aviation concern have signed a letter of intent to start assembly of F-16 multi-purpose fighter aircraft at Mielec if Lockheed Martin wins the tender to supply aircraft to the Polish military, the companies said.
- Korean firms have expressed interest in the planned special economic zone in Lodz, central Poland, to be discusssed by the cabinet today.
Companies ready to invest in the zone will receive up to 20 year tax breaks, the treasury ministry said.
- Poland and the EU will liberalise trade in confectionery products and cut import duties in the next few months, a recent agreement in Brussels said.

- The Martin Bauer group, controlling several international herb processing firms, has invested 13 million zlotys in modernisation of its Polish subsidiary Herbabol Kleka, Herbapol president Jerzy Jambor said.

- The general shareholders meeting of the PEC heating energy supplier in Kalisz, central Poland, has decided to increase share capital and issue shares addressed to French strategic investor, the Thion heating energy group, and create a Polish-French joint venture called Interpec with a founding capital of $630,000.
- The prices of Fiat cars produced and assembled in Poland inched up by 2.5 percent on April 4 due to production cost growth caused by inflation, Fiat Auto Poland official Maciej Brzozowski said.

- Austria's Creditanstalt Financial Advisers SA acted as an adviser in 20 privatisations in its first five years of operations in Poland. The combined value of the sales totalled $900 million, the company said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- Korea's Daewoo car manufacturer plans to start assemblying new passenger car models: Lanos, Nubira, the new Espero model and V100 limousine model by the end of this year, Daewoo-FSO financial director Janusz Maciej Lach said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Polskie Centrum Leasingowe leasing firm has offered to lease Mercedes and Jelcz buses from Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum (SZC) automotive group to urban transport firms.
The Warsaw urban transport firm could lease 490 new buses instead of financing costly maintenance of old vehicles.
ZYCIE

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the Bank of America are considering investing in the Hortex fruit and vegetable processing firm, a source which declined to be named said.
PARKIET
- The Czech Skoda truck maker has expressed interest in buying a stake in the ZS Star truck plant in Starachowice, southern Poland.
Previously, the Sobieslaw Zasada Centrum automotive group disclosed plans to participate in the plant's privatisation.
